newsitem.title: USA: DAKOTAH SEES NO AUG IMPACT FROM UPS STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: DAKOTAH SEES NO AUG IMPACT FROM UPS STRIKE.

text.p: Dakotah Inc said on Thursday the current United Parcel Service strike would not have a significant adverse impact on August sales or earnings.

"While we ship nearly all of our smaller shipments via UPS, well over 95 percent of August shipments are scheduled to use common carriers," Troy Jones Jr, chief executive of the home accessory product company, said.

However, if the strike extends into late September or October, it might affect shipments to Dakotah's gift-store customers unless other arrangements were made, Jones said, adding that he intended to make alternative plans before then.
Additionally, the company has chosen to delay implementation of its new comprehensive computer and information software package until the first quarter of 1998.
The company also said it finalized a $15 million credit facility with Diversified Business Credit Inc, a subsidiary of National City Bank, NA.
The new credit facility, which expires June 30, 1999, consists of a $13 million of secured revolving credit and a $2 million secured term loan agreement.
It replaces a temporary $11 million secured revolving credit agreement and $600,000 secured term loan with Norwest Business Credit Inc, a subsidiary of Norwest Corp, the company said.
Dakotah shares closed up 1/16 at 2-7/8 Thursday.
